svg.aria-label: Graph BFS/DFS mechanism map: the visited-set discipline, and eight variant diagrams.
svg.text: A tree never revisits a node, so tree traversal never needed a visited set. A graph can
have cycles — without tracking what's been seen, DFS or BFS on one loops forever.
A cycle, without a visited set, loops forever
DFS walks A → B → C. C's edge back to A isn't a new place to explore — it's the same
node, reached a second time. The visited set is what makes that obvious.
One visited-set discipline, eight different uses

g.text: Each cell is a node; adjacent
cells are its edges. Mark visited
looked up in an adjacency list
both sources expand together, minute by minute
Every source starts in the queue
covers all of them at once.
first time E is dequeued = shortest path
The visited map's value IS the
clone — a cycle just reuses it
C → A: A visited AND not parent → cycle
both ways, so the node you came
A finished node can be reached
again safely — only a node still
on the call stack is a real cycle.
